paths.learner_scope: Beginner-to-job-ready, entry/junior-level learners with general computer literacy; no prior programming experience is silently assumed. Required Python fundamentals remain explicit learner coverage: where equivalent foundations already exist in this run's global_concept_registry_snapshot.json, schedule them as prerequisite coverage through the registry delta rather than creating duplicate concepts. Teach missing Python and type-hint skills natively. Apply the same reuse rule to SQL and relational-model foundations. Delegate Git, systematic debugging methodology, code review and CI/CD-purpose coverage to registered Software Engineer prerequisites before the tasks that need them; do not assume completion of an entire unrelated path. Progress from foundations and mental models to basic usage, integration and professional delivery. Binding scope: target 120 final atomic concepts, hard ceiling 140, with the Stage 03 candidate inventory already within the ceiling; about six per benchmark family and never more than nine. Use only the benchmark's 20 capability families. Admit only first-six-month unaided job capabilities; preserve atomic size and cut breadth, not required capabilities, when fitting the budget.

inline_vocabulary.definition: OpenAPI security must describe the actually deployed bearer and authorization-code/PKCE contract, never present the tutorial password grant as production guidance.
OpenAPI describes how clients obtain and present accepted authority.
Public security documentation describes the actual deployed bearer and established issuer contract, not a password grant.

concepts.primary_objective: Document the deployed API authentication contract
concepts.assessment_target: Detect security documentation that misrepresents the deployed bearer or authorization-code flow
concepts.practice_objective: Document one deployed bearer scheme and established authorization-server flow without a password grant
concepts.central_mental_model: OpenAPI security declares how clients obtain and present the authority the deployed service actually accepts.
